title: Hestia: the goddess with no stories who was everything in Rome
cover:
Hestia: almost no stories…
and the fire of Troy

scenes.text: A Greek goddess with almost no stories. And in Rome, keeper of the fire of Troy.
Hestia is the firstborn of Cronus: the first child he swallows… and the last he spits back out.
Poseidon and Apollo both seek her hand. She touches the head of Zeus and swears to stay a maiden forever.
Her reward: the centre of the house. And at every banquet, wine is poured to her, first and last.
And that's nearly all. The Greek texts give her no more story. Not even priests.
Now, Rome. Vesta has the Vestal Virgins: Numa gives them a public salary and makes them untouchable.
Her fire comes from Troy: Hector's ghost hands it to Aeneas as the city burns.
And the mother of Romulus, Rhea Silvia, was a Vestal.
So they're the same goddess by function: hearth and virginity. But they share not a single myth.
Before you call them the same goddess, ask: which text says so?
Save it, and send it to anyone who thinks Vesta is just the Roman Hestia.
